Title: Melaka polls: Anwar appeals armed forces, police personnel to back PH
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Pakatan Harapan chairman Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has appealed to armed forces and police personnel voting early in the Melaka election tomorrow to place their trust in PH candidates.
In a Facebook post, the prime minister said the mandate entrusted to PH candidates would be upheld with commitment and determination to serve all Melaka residents.
"Tomorrow, our friends and families from the armed forces and police will fulfil their responsibilities as early voters in Melaka.
"With humility, I appeal for your trust by voting for Harapan candidates.
"Your votes will determine whether Melaka is led by those who stand firm in upholding the people's trust or those who are willing to turn a blind eye when that trust is betrayed. To Allah, we surrender," he added.
A total of 12,531 eligible early voters, comprising 9,769 military personnel and their spouses and 2,762 police personnel will cast their ballots across 31 gazetted early polling centres statewide tomorrow.
Overall, 687,697 electors are eligible to vote in the state election.
The Election Commission has set polling day for Nov 14.

Title: Pahang Sultan opens Malaysia Pavilion at COP31 in Turkiye
Article:
KUANTAN: The Sultan of Pahang, Al-Sultan Abdullah Ri'ayatuddin Al-Mustafa Billah Shah, today officiated the opening of the Malaysia Pavilion at the 31st Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (COP31) in Antalya, Turkiye.
Tengku Ampuan Pahang Tunku Azizah Aminah Maimunah Iskandariah was also in attendance.
The Pahang Sultanate said in a Facebook post that the event is part of Malaysia's participation in the international conference, hosted by Turkiye from Nov 9 to 20.
"Their Royal Highnesses' presence reflects their support for efforts to strengthen the environmental sustainability agenda, the preservation of natural treasures, and international cooperation to ensure sustainable development for current and future generations," the post read.
The COP31 conference gathers world leaders, government representatives, international organisations, and various stakeholders to strengthen global cooperation in tackling climate change and accelerate the implementation of existing climate action commitments.
According to the post, the Malaysia Pavilion serves as a platform to highlight the country's efforts in the climate change agenda, while providing a space to share experiences, exchange views, and foster cooperation with the international community.
Also on the COP31 agenda are efforts to strengthen the Global Zero Waste Alliance through voluntary cooperation among nations, international organisations, local authorities, the private sector, and civil society to expand sustainable waste management practices and the circular economy.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Four students caught cheating using AI glasses at middle, high schools in South Korea
Article:
SEOUL: Four cases of cheating using artificial intelligence (AI) glasses have been reported at middle and high schools this year, South Korea's Education Ministry said on Monday, Yonhap News Agency reported.
According to data collected from all 5,679 middle and high schools nationwide between Oct 27 and last Tuesday, one middle school student and three high school students were caught using AI glasses during their midterm or final examinations.
The middle school and one high school are in Seoul, while the two other high schools are in North Jeolla Province and the southern island of Jeju.
Three of the four students were caught repeatedly touching their glasses, while the other was caught switching to AI glasses after the examination had begun. In the latter case, the invigilator had been keeping a close eye on the student following a tip-off from another student, officials said.
All four students received zero marks for the affected examinations in accordance with relevant regulations.
In addition, separate disciplinary measures were taken against the three high school students, including three days of special education, four hours of community service and a five-day suspension. The middle school student did not face any official disciplinary action but was asked to perform volunteer work on campus.
The Education Ministry said it planned to distribute educational materials to students detailing these cheating cases, along with guidelines for schools to prevent the misuse of AI glasses.
The ministry added that it would discuss further preventive measures with regional education offices and the Korea Institute for Curriculum and Evaluation (KICE).
The ministry earlier said those caught cheating in the annual college entrance examination using AI glasses would face criminal charges and be barred from taking the test for three years, up from the current one-year ban.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Lawyers for Philippine VP Duterte open defence in high-stakes trial
Article:
MANILA: Philippine Vice-President Sara Duterte's lawyers on Monday sought to counter allegations that she had accumulated unexplained wealth, opening their defence in a high-profile impeachment trial in which a conviction would end her hopes of becoming president.
The daughter of firebrand former leader Rodrigo Duterte has consistently been the frontrunner in opinion polls to win the presidency in 2028. Her defence must win over at least one-third of senators in the impeachment court to guarantee her political survival.
The prosecution's case centres on allegations that Duterte amassed wealth beyond what could be explained by her declared income and assets, after it withdrew three other charges included in the impeachment complaint against her.
The defence on Monday called the first of its 24 witnesses, Jaime Adalin, an assessor in Duterte's hometown of Davao City, to rebut what it called a "malicious and completely false" prosecution claim that a property linked to her was missing from her asset declarations.
Adalin testified about tax declarations and assessment records that the defence said supported its argument that the property had been disclosed in Duterte's 2024 statement of assets and liabilities.
The defence plans to call accountants, bankers and corporate counsel for Duterte-linked firms as part of its case and hopes the trial can be concluded by year-end.
A forensic financial analyst who testified for the prosecution last month estimated that Duterte had more than 800 million pesos (US$12.70 million) in unexplained assets, including remittances from entities in China and Hong Kong.
Duterte has called the proceedings political harassment and denied wrongdoing.
She has stayed away from the trial since proceedings began in July, apart from a brief appearance on the second day, when she declared herself "bloodied but unbowed".
While prosecutors have challenged Duterte to take the witness stand, defence spokesman Michael Poa said on Monday it was too early to say whether the vice-president would testify.
Her impeachment was the biggest escalation in a political conflict between Duterte and President Ferdinand Marcos Jr, who were powerful allies when they ran on a joint ticket and swept the 2022 election before their relationship soured.
Marcos, who is limited to a single term in office, has said the impeachment is a legislative matter.
In a separate criminal case, Duterte is also accused of three counts of grave threats linked to comments she made about Marcos, the first lady and a former House speaker. She denies wrongdoing.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Home Ministry leaves conflicting interpretations over Najib's house arrest issue to court
Article:
MELAKA: The Home Ministry is leaving it to the courts to resolve conflicting interpretations of the law concerning the implementation of house arrest for former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak.
Its minister, Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail, said the issue concerned the use of the term 'Order of Discharge' in a court order, as opposed to the Pardons Board's decision, which he said stipulated that Najib serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest.
He said the ministry had never disputed the Pardons Board's decision but required legal clarification to ensure that any action taken complied with the proper procedures and fell within the relevant authorities' jurisdiction.
"If there are two interpretations, the court is the best platform to resolve them. The ministry will abide by and respect that process.
"The only matter we need to resolve now is whether there is a need to clarify these two differing interpretations first.
"As for the Yang di-Pertuan Agong's decree, nobody is questioning that," he told reporters after attending an engagement session with fishermen at the Sungai Lereh Fishermen's Jetty in Klebang here today.
Also present was Malaysian Fisheries Development Authority chairman Muhammad Faiz Fadzil.
On Friday, Umno confirmed that the RM50 million fine imposed on Najib had been paid at the Kuala Lumpur High Court, paving the way for the implementation of house arrest under the terms of the conditional pardon granted to him.
However, the implementation of house arrest was put on hold after the Attorney-General's Chambers (AGC) announced that it wanted to conduct further clarification on the interpretation of the Conditional
Pardon Order and the implications of the High Court's Order of Discharge
issued after the fine was paid.
Following this, Attorney-General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar sought
an audience with the Yang di-Pertuan Agong
to explain his position on compliance with the royal decree concerning Najib's Conditional Pardon Order.
Saifuddin said the confusion arose from the use of the term 'Order of Discharge', which meant release, whereas the implementation of house arrest required the Prisons Department to retain authority over the prisoner.
He said that if the order was interpreted as a full discharge, the Prisons Department would no longer have jurisdiction over Najib.
However, if the Pardons Board's decision were implemented in the form of house arrest, the residence concerned would have to be gazetted to enable Najib to serve the remainder of his sentence under the supervision of the Prisons Department.
"House arrest is one thing, discharge is another. So, from our position, which one should we follow? These are legal documents and legal terms. Our country has laws, and if there is any confusion, we refer the matter to the court," he said.
Saifuddin said the ministry was taking a cautious approach as any misinterpretation of the order could have legal implications, including the possibility of wrongful detention.
"Imagine if the court rules that it is a discharge, meaning the Prisons Department must release Datuk Seri Najib, but instead we send him to house arrest. That could amount to wrongful detention.
"For now, let the court decide, as there are differing interpretations," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Three stations in Terengganu record over 100mm of rain
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Three weather monitoring stations in Terengganu recorded more than 100 mm of rain within 12 hours, with the highest reading of 183.1mm recorded in Cendering.
The other two stations were Kuala Tengah in Marang, which recorded 130.2mm, and Felda Belara, with 100.2mm, between 1am and 1pm today.
Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) deputy director-general (operations) Ambun Dindang said the readings had prompted the continuous rain warning to be raised to orange level in several areas in Kelantan and Terengganu.
"Several other stations in Terengganu and Kelantan also recorded rainfall above 50mm as of 1pm today.
"Rain clouds are still moving into the two states, and we expect rainfall could exceed 150mm within 24 hours.
"That is among the criteria for us to raise the warning to the orange level," he said when contacted.
Ambun said the orange warning issued today covered Bachok, Kota Baru, Tumpat, Pasir Mas and Pasir Puteh in Kelantan, and Besut, Setiu, Dungun, Kemaman, Marang, Kuala Terengganu and Kuala Nerus in Terengganu.
The warning is expected to remain in force until Nov 11.
He said MetMalaysia had initially issued an "Alert" level continuous rain warning on Nov 6, effective from Nov 8 to 11, before updating it yesterday to include coastal areas in Pahang, as well as Kemaman and Dungun.
On flood preparedness, Ambun advised residents to remain alert throughout the northeast monsoon, which began on Oct 27.
"Residents in areas that flood often, particularly in Kelantan and Terengganu, need to stay aware of weather conditions throughout this northeast monsoon.
"If rain continues for more than a day, they must be ready to be evacuated and follow the authorities' instructions so that evacuation can be carried out earlier," he said.

Title: Steel plant blast kills 3, leaves 10 missing in western Turkiye [WATCH]
Article:
ANKARA: An explosion at an iron and steel manufacturing plant in western Turkiye on Monday killed three people, left 10 missing and injured 14 others, the local governor's office said.
The explosion occurred at around noon (0900 GMT) at the Habas iron and steel manufacturing plant in the Aliaga district of Izmir province, the governor's office said in a statement.
According to initial findings, the incident happened when a ceiling crane snapped and fell into an arc furnace during the liquid steel casting process.
Footage broadcast by local television stations showed large plumes of grey dust rising above the plant.
Those injured were taken to various hospitals in the region for treatment. Three of the 14 injured were in a serious condition, according to the statement.
Search and rescue operations were under way to reach the 10 people still trapped under the rubble after the explosion.

Title: Spanish investigators slam TikTok's inaction on child abuse
Article:
MADRID: A Spanish anti-disinformation foundation accused TikTok on Monday of failing to do enough to prevent paedophiles from accessing child sexual abuse material or soliciting images from children on the platform.
"Material you would expect to find only on the dark web is on TikTok," the Maldita.es association said.
In an investigation published on Monday, Maldita.es catalogued more than 1,000 videos containing child abuse footage, which had been viewed a total of 48 million times.
"The findings of this investigation seriously call into question the effectiveness of TikTok's measures against child abuse, and also point directly to its platform features being actively exploited by child predators," the association said.
TikTok had yet to respond to an AFP request for comment.
According to Maldita.es, TikTok removed only one-tenth of the content it had flagged and blocked just 26 per cent of illegal posts in Spain.
The widely popular platform, owned by Chinese parent company ByteDance, faces a wave of lawsuits and investigations over accusations that it has failed to protect minors, which the company has frequently denied.
On Friday, the EU told TikTok to change the "harmful" design of its personalised For You feed or risk large fines under the bloc's digital content rules.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka polls: 12,531 early voters to cast ballots tomorrow
Article:
MELAKA: A total of 12,531 eligible early voters in the 16th Melaka election will cast their ballots at 31 gazetted polling centres statewide tomorrow.
They comprise 9,769 military personnel and their spouses, and 2,762 police personnel.
All polling centres will open at 8am and close at staggered times between noon and 6pm, depending on their locations and the number of registered voters.
Several centres with smaller electorates, including the Masjid Tanah police station for the Lendu state constituency and the Gadek police station for the Gadek state constituency, are scheduled to close as early as noon.
Polling centres at the Melaka contingent police headquarters, Alor Gajah district police headquarters and SK Kem Terendak 1 are scheduled to close at 6pm.
Overall, 687,697 voters are eligible to vote in the state election.
Pakatan Harapan is fielding candidates in 24 state seats, followed by Barisan Nasional (23), Parti Bersama Malaysia (16), Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (seven), Perikatan Nasional (five), Parti Pribumi Perkasa Malaysia (one) and three Independents.
In the 2021 Melaka state election, Barisan Nasional won 21 seats to form the state government, while Pakatan Harapan won five and Perikatan Nasional two.
The Election Commission has set polling day for Nov 14.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Rantau Panjang traders cut stock, move goods ahead of annual floods
Article:
PASIR MAS: The annual threat of flooding has prompted traders in Rantau Panjang to take extra precautions, including reducing stock levels and moving merchandise to higher ground to minimise losses during the monsoon season.
Clothing trader Azila Zanuddin, 45, said most traders were avoiding large purchases of new stock as they normally would towards the end of the year, opting instead to sell existing merchandise before gradually replenishing their supplies.
"It has become a necessity for us traders here towards the end of the year, as the monsoon season approaches.
"We store our merchandise in higher places to prevent damage and losses.
"Likewise, most traders avoid purchasing large quantities of new stock during the monsoon season. We sell our existing stock first, before gradually replenishing our supplies in smaller quantities," she told Bernama.
Another trader, Muhammad Shahmir Amzar Azmi, 25, who sells shoes and slippers, said he was taking precautionary measures by moving his merchandise to a specially built loft at his business premises, to prevent damage in the event of floodwaters entering his shop.
"These preparations are necessary every year, as we do not want to take any chances in the event of sudden flooding.
"Goods which are easily damaged and those of high value will be moved to higher places first, while other items are arranged so that they can be easily relocated if the situation worsens," he said.
He said business equipment and important documents were also kept in safe places in preparation for possible flooding.
Checks by Bernama found that most traders in the town had begun making early preparations for the monsoon season, including moving their merchandise to higher places and setting up storage areas, to minimise the risk of losses.
Meanwhile, residents in several flood-prone villages around Rantau Panjang, including Kampung Gual Periok, Kampung Padang Lincin and Kampung Tok Deh, have also taken early precautionary measures, by preparing fibreglass boats for use as transport during floods.
A resident, Shukri Che Mat, 60, said the fibreglass boats would be used to facilitate residents' movement when floodwaters inundated the village.
"Floodwaters usually rise to chest level in this village, as it is located just a few metres from Golok River.
"Water levels typically rise after two or three hours of continuous heavy rain. Therefore, to avoid a chaotic situation, we make early preparations by moving essential items to higher places," he said.
Meanwhile, checks in several areas around Kota Baru found that the weather had remained overcast from morning until late afternoon today, with no sunshine and intermittent showers occurring at short intervals.

Title: Bangladesh challenges ousted PM Hasina over return pledge
Article:
DHAKA: Bangladesh challenged ousted leader Sheikh Hasina on Monday to seek extradition from India if she was serious about returning home, while reviewing an application to renew her passport.
Hasina, whose 15-year rule was ended by a mass uprising she tried to crush, has vowed to return to Bangladesh in December. She was sentenced to death for crimes against humanity over the 2024 crackdown on protesters.
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed told reporters on Monday that authorities were looking into Hasina's request for a new passport, adding that she was a convicted offender who had taken refuge abroad.
"The legal basis of the application, whether it followed due process, and whether there is a right to apply for a passport – all those matters are being reviewed," he said.
"We had already sent a letter to that country (India) seeking her extradition through due process," he added.
Hasina has said several times that she intends to return, telling AFP in an email that she was "fully aware" she faced being hanged.
Hasina's British lawyers have requested the renewal of her documents following the "reported revocation" of her passport.
A letter by law firm Matrix Chambers, addressed to Bangladesh's high commission in New Delhi and seen by AFP, requested the renewal of her passport but made no mention of when or where she planned to travel.
Md Aminul Islam, chief prosecutor of the court that sentenced Hasina to death in November 2025, dismissed the application as "nothing but political stunt".
Humaiun Kobir, Bangladesh's junior foreign minister, said she should simply surrender herself to face justice.
"Let her tell India: 'Yes, there is an extradition treaty. Please hand me over. I killed this many people, and I am ready to face the sentence. Please execute me there'," he told reporters.
"She is a thief, a bandit and a terrorist who fled... How could she, having fled, want to come back?"
Trying to create panic
Hasina fled to old ally India in 2024 and has not been seen in public since, but has taken part in online news conferences by telephone.
She was convicted and sentenced in absentia.
Her continued presence in India has strained ties between Dhaka and New Delhi, which says the extradition request is under legal review.
The government of Tarique Rahman, whose party won elections in February in which Hasina's Awami League was barred from contesting, has said it would ensure the former prime minister receives due legal process in all cases against her should she return.
But Hasina's pledge to return presents a political challenge for Rahman's government.
Many Bangladeshis want to see her hanged, while others fear her return could galvanise her former supporters and trigger a fresh confrontation between rival camps.
Police on Monday said they had arrested 12 people over a series of petrol bomb attacks this month, including attacks on property, an empty bus and police vehicles. No casualties were reported.
Dhaka police spokesman Md Akhtar Hossain said the suspects were members of Hasina's banned Awami League party.
"They are trying to create panic among people," he told AFP. "We are remaining vigilant to deal with any untoward situation."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Teens aged 16 and 18 among three killed by lightning strike in Sepang
Article:
SEPANG: Two teenagers aged 16 and 18 were among three men killed after they were believed to have been struck by lightning while taking shelter under a tree in Bandar Baru Salak Tinggi.
Sepang police chief Assistant Commissioner Norhizam Bahaman said the third victim was a 26-year-old man.
He said all three victims had been taken to Serdang Hospital for further action.
Earlier, Norhizam c
onfirmed the incident
when contacted.
"At the time, the victims were repairing a car and taking shelter under a tree when they were believed to have been struck by lightning during the rain," he said.
Several videos showing three bodies covered with batik cloth beneath a tree went viral on social media.
The photographs and videos were uploaded by residents and motorists passing through the area.
The exact time of the incident has yet to be officially confirmed.

Title: Negri Sembilan assembly sitting without ruler's consent could trigger constitutional crisis – analyst
Article:
SEREMBAN: Plans to convene the Negri Sembilan state assembly on Nov 26 without the consent of Yang di-Pertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir could trigger a serious constitutional and administrative crisis, a constitutional law expert has warned.
Universiti Teknologi Mara (UiTM) Negri Sembilan senior lecturer Dr Muhamad Fuad Abdul Karim said there was a clear legal distinction between an official opening ceremony and royal consent.
He said the state assembly could proceed without Tuanku Muhriz physically officiating the opening, as the absence of a royal address would not invalidate its proceedings.
"However, the state assembly cannot convene without Tuanku Muhriz's formal consent through an instrument of summons.
"Without it, the planned Nov 26 sitting would not merely be inappropriate, but invalid.
"If it goes ahead, it would be an unprecedented event," he said when contacted.
The sitting is scheduled for Nov 26, with the 2027 state Budget set to be tabled the following day.
However, the state government has yet to obtain Tuanku Muhriz's consent to convene the sitting.
This follows the State Executive Council's decision to recognise the April 19 proclamation concerning Tuanku Muhriz's removal as Yang di-Pertuan Besar as valid and effective.
Earlier, Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim said the state government would proceed with its original plan to convene the sitting on Nov 26, followed by the tabling of the 2027 state Budget a day later.
The Juasseh assemblyman said the state government was working to obtain Tuanku Muhriz's consent to officiate the sitting.
Fuad said proceeding with the sitting without resolving the constitutional issues could paralyse its functions.
"Even if the sitting meets the minimum quorum, the absence of exco members could hamper the state government's executive functions.
"The tabling of the 2027 state Budget could also be affected as the menteri besar does not have the constitutional authority to approve budget policies on his own before presenting them to the state assembly," he said.
He said question-and-answer sessions could also be disrupted, as the menteri besar would have to answer questions across portfolios, including religious affairs, housing, the economy and infrastructure, which would normally be handled by the respective exco members.
He said the sitting should not proceed without the proper constitutional procedures being followed.
"The state government must resolve the appointment of a legitimate Exco line-up in accordance with constitutional requirements.
"It must also formally seek and obtain Tuanku Muhriz's consent before issuing any notice to convene the sitting," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Food delivery rider held for peeping into women's toilet at Bukit Bintang mall
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A food delivery rider has been arrested for peeping into a women's toilet at a Bukit Bintang mall.
Dang Wangi police chief Assistant Commissioner Ahmad Azwan Amin Nordin said a 37-year-old woman was using a cubicle when she realised someone was peeping at her from above.
"She screamed and called out to her husband for help," he said in a statement.
Police later arrested the suspect at the scene. The 21-year-old man has been remanded for three days.
The case is being investigated under Section 509 of the Penal Code and Section 14 of the Minor Offences Act for insulting a person's modesty and insulting behaviour.
If convicted, the man could face a five-year jail term, fines, or both.
"Those with information on the case can contact Kuala Lumpur police at 03-2146 0522 or 03-2146 0585, Dang Wangi police at 03-2600 2222, or visit any nearby police station," he said.
Earlier, photos and video clips went viral showing members of the public confronting the suspect before police arrived.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Olympic judo champion Riner joins fight for French presidency
Article:
PARIS: France's five-time Olympic judo champion Teddy Riner announced on Monday that he would run in next year's presidential election, after expressing concern about the "rise of the far right".
"My name is Teddy Riner and today, I am telling you face to face: I am a candidate in the 2027 presidential election," the 37-year-old said in a surprise announcement on social media.
Riner, one of France's best-known sports figures, enters the race with far-right presidential candidate Marine Le Pen leading in the polls to replace centrist President Emmanuel Macron next year.
The judo star has publicly said he was very worried about the "rise of the far right" in France.
Le Pen's anti-immigration party emerged as the single largest party in the National Assembly after Macron called snap polls in 2024, though it fell well short of a majority.
It increased its seats from three to at least 15 in the 348-seat Senate in elections in September.
"Fighting has always been part of me," said Riner, who hails from the French overseas territory of Guadeloupe.
"I know what it means to fight, to fall, to always get back up," the judoka said, sitting in front of a bookcase and wearing a white shirt and dark jacket.
"I know what people are going to say about me: 'He's crazy. He's not from the establishment. He doesn't have the codes. He's never done politics,'" he added.
"If refusing to bow my head and refusing chaos makes me crazy, then yes, I'm completely crazy."
Olympian and president?
In an interview with Le Parisien newspaper, Riner said he intended to continue his sports career alongside his presidential bid.
If elected president, he said he planned to compete in the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, "if the position allows me to, and if the French people allow me to".
Riner won the heavyweight division at the 2012, 2016 and 2024 Olympics and mixed team gold at the 2020 and 2024 Games.
He has also won 11 world titles.
Another French judo star, David Douillet, was elected to the French parliament in 2009 and served as sports minister from September 2011 to May 2012.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PN, Pas insist 'Muafakat Melaka' pact with BN is built to last
Article:
MELAKA: Perikatan Nasional (PN) and Pas leaders have defended their electoral cooperation with Barisan Nasional (BN), dismissing criticism that the partnership is fragile or one-sided.
Melaka Pas chairman Zulkifli Ismail dismissed remarks by Amanah president Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu, who claimed that previous ties between Umno and Pas had never lasted more than three years.
"That is just the view of people who do not want to see this unity work," Zulkifli said at a press conference to present the aspirations of PN candidates for the 16th Melaka election.
"Those of us working on the ground are not planning for three years (only). We want to make sure this partnership lasts for good."
Zulkifli also rejected claims that Umno was playing both sides, describing them as unfair attacks intended to score political points.
With the campaign entering its final days, he said the coalition was focusing on rallies across all 28 state constituencies, culminating in a prayer gathering and a final rally before polling day.
Tangga Batu member of parliament and PN Melaka election director Bakri Jamaluddin dismissed claims that PN was being sidelined by BN under the 'Muafakat Melaka' banner.
"Working together means give and take. It does not mean being bullied," he said.
"We have put together a joint manifesto with six main areas and 113 initiatives, including plans for the first 100 days, one year and five years to bring jobs and investment to Melaka.
"We are looking at the bigger picture for stability here and across the country," he added.
PN Bemban candidate Dr Mohd Yadzil Yaakub said relations among party members on the ground went beyond party affiliations.
"Our relationship is not based on party lines, but on sincerity and doing what is right. That is why it is easy to work together," he said, adding that the team would continue working hard until polling day.

Title: Toddler missing after falling into river in Gopeng, search underway
Article:
IPOH: A 2-year-and-10-month-old boy is feared drowned after falling into a river during a family outing at Dataran Sungai Jahang, Kampung Jahang, near Gopeng, around noon today.
Perak Fire and Rescue Department Operations Division assistant director Sabarodzi Nor Ahmad said a team from the Gopeng Fire and Rescue Station was dispatched to the scene after receiving a  call at 12.06pm.
"The search involved the police, villagers and a nearby tour company, which assisted by providing eight rafting boats.
"By 3.45 pm, search teams extended their initial search to a distance of four kilometres from the location where the victim was reported to have fallen," he said in a statement.
He said the search area was being expanded this afternoon, with a control post already set up at the scene.
Personnel from the Kampar Fire and Rescue Station were also assisting by monitoring the river downstream near Kampar, he said, adding that the search is still ongoing.
In a separate incident at Pulau Pangkor, a 38-year-old Myanmar was feared drowned after suffering a seizure and falling into the sea.
Sabarodzi said the department received an emergency call at 12.54pm before a team from the Pangkor Fire and Rescue Station was dispatched to the scene.
"Upon arrival, the operations commander was informed that the man had suffered a seizure while aboard a boat moored at the jetty before falling into the sea.
"The search operation is ongoing," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Driver charged with DUI causes another crash while testing positive for drugs
Article:
KUALA PILAH: A driver who previously tested positive for drugs in an accident involving five vehicles was arrested after being involved in another crash along Jalan Seremban-Kuala Pilah near Tanjong Ipoh on Saturday.
Kuala Pilah police chief Superintendent Muhamad Mustafah Hussin said the 2.45pm accident was believed to have occurred when a Toyota Vios driven by the 39-year-old suspect, travelling from Seremban towards Bahau, rammed into the rear of a Nissan Grand Livina.
He said the impact caused the Nissan Grand Livina to skid forward before hitting a Proton Wira.
"Urine screening found substances suspected to be MDMA and Eramin 5. The suspect was arrested and taken to the Kuala Pilah police headquarters for further investigation," he said in a statement.
Mustafah said the suspect had previously been charged under Section 44(1A) of the Road Transport Act for driving under the influence of drugs, resulting in injuries to other road users.
No injuries were reported among the drivers involved in Saturday's accident, although all three vehicles were damaged.

Title: Nacsa records 5,110 cybersecurity incidents in first nine months
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The National Cyber Security Agency (Nacsa) recorded 5,110 cybersecurity incidents from January to September this year, compared with 5,837 for the whole of last year.
Nacsa chief executive Dr Megat Zuhairy Megat Tajuddin said the higher figure last year was largely driven by intrusion attempts and potential attacks detected at an early stage.
He said Nacsa's National Cyber Coordination and Command Centre (NC4) also issued nine alerts and advisories in October and November this year, concerning security vulnerabilities affecting National Critical Information Infrastructure (NCII) entities and government agencies.
"It is important to understand that not all cybersecurity incidents have the same impact, and Nacsa's main focus is on incidents which have the potential to disrupt the country's essential services," he told Bernama.
He said the cybersecurity incidents recorded included a ransomware attack on Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd in March 2025, which caused disruptions at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) for more than 10 hours.
Commenting on the viral Live Map & Ranking display, which placed Malaysia among the countries receiving the highest number of cyber attacks, Megat Zuhairy said the figures were based on monitoring through specific cyber security products and platforms, widely used by organisations in Malaysia.
"The sensors installed enable proactive monitoring of detected cyber activities and traffic, providing an overview based on data from these sources.
"Additionally, Malaysia is one of the key data centre hubs globally, and this position means that a large volume of international internet traffic passes through the country, either as a target of cyber attacks, or as a transit route to other destinations," he said.
Megat Zuhairy said the display did not reflect the overall cyber security situation of a country, as a comprehensive assessment would need to take into account various other factors and data sources.
These include actual cyber security incidents, as detected activities or attempted attacks do not necessarily mean that an organisation has experienced an incident or system breach.
He said there was currently no specific global ranking or report comparing countries, based on actual cyber attack incidents.
However, based on the National Cyber Threat Level (NCTL) assessment, Malaysia's cyber threat level remained moderate, while the country was placed in Tier 1 under the Global Cybersecurity Index (GCI).
He added that Malaysia was also preparing for the transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC), to address developments in quantum computing technology.
Megat Zuhairy said individuals were also targets of cyber threats, particularly through the hacking of social media, email and online banking accounts.
He reminded the public to understand the difference between account hacking and online scams, so that appropriate action could be taken if they encountered such situations.
"Hacking occurs when another party gains unauthorised access to an account or system.
"Early warning signs include login notifications from unrecognised devices or locations, passwords being changed without the account owner's knowledge, or messages being sent from one's own account without authorisation.
"Scams, on the other hand, occur when victims are deceived into voluntarily handing over money or information, for example, through calls, messages or fake offers," he said.
Megat Zuhairy also urged users whose accounts had been compromised to immediately change their passwords, activate multi-factor authentication (MFA) and report the matter to the relevant platform provider.
Victims of scams involving money transfers, meanwhile, should contact their banks and the National Scam Response Centre (NSRC) via its hotline at 997.
"Authentic precautionary measures are generally simple and practical, such as activating MFA, keeping devices updated and refraining from sharing personal information.
"The public should also be wary of posts which do not cite clear sources, use an urgent tone, or recommend drastic measures such as withdrawing all their savings," he said.

Title: Three Malaysians held in Mauritius with 76kg of cannabis
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Three Malaysians were arrested upon arrival in Mauritius on Nov 2 after authorities found 76.14kg of cannabis in their luggage.
The trio comprised two men, aged 22 and 30, and an 18-year-old woman.
The Mauritius Revenue Authority (MRA) said the Malaysians arrived at Sir Seewoosagur Ramgoolam International Airport on Nov 2 before being flagged for further checks.
A search of their luggage found 70 rectangular, vacuum-packed black plastic parcels containing green plant material suspected to be cannabis.
The seized drugs are estimated to be worth 114.21 million Mauritian rupees (about RM9.87 million).
"All parcels were seized, and further investigations are being carried out by the Anti-Drug and Smuggling Unit," the MRA said.
Mauritius media reported that preliminary investigations linked the drugs to Thailand, with one of the suspects believed to have transited through the country before flying to Dubai and then Mauritius.
The 30-year-old man, who reportedly lives and works as a security officer in Singapore, was found carrying about 10.9kg of the drug.
The other two suspects, a 22-year-old man and an 18-year-old woman, were carrying 32.5kg and 32.6kg respectively.
A similar modus operandi was detected on Oct 23, when a 55-year-old Malaysian cook was arrested at the airport with 17.8kg of cannabis in his luggage.
The man had also arrived from Dubai.

Title: With Stephen Miller at the helm, Trump charts a course for conflict
Article:
PRESIDENT Donald Trump's decision to elevate loyalist Stephen Miller to run his White House indicates that he plans to ramp up confrontation in his final two years in office and block outside political and economic pressures, Trump administration officials and other Republicans say.
Voters delivered a historic rebuke to Republicans in Tuesday's midterm election, but with Miller as White House chief of staff, the Trump administration is expected to continue its aggressive immigration crackdown, amplify cultural conflicts and give no ground to a Democratic-controlled Congress.
They say wavering Republicans will face increased pressure to stay in line, while businesses may have a harder time making their case to the White House.
"This signals the administration is going to have a fighting-from-a-bunker approach the last two years," said Dan Eberhart, a Trump donor and energy executive.
Although Trump has said he can work with Democrats, he has shown a feisty approach since the midterm election results became clear.
On Saturday he ordered the Justice Department to "look into" Democrats whom he accused of sending "threatening letters" to Republican donors and other Trump allies.
Miller, 41, marks a sharp contrast with outgoing chief of staff Susie Wiles, a former lobbyist who ran Trump's 2024 presidential campaign.
Wiles lacked significant Washington experience but was seen as a deft manager of competing interests. Miller, by contrast, is regarded by allies and foes alike as a combative ideologue with an unswerving loyalty to Trump.
"If it wasn't for President Trump, the United States of America would not exist right now. This man saved America," Miller said at an event at Trump's Florida estate on Friday.
Miller joined Trump's first presidential campaign in 2016 and served throughout his two terms in the White House. He is best known for driving Trump's aggressive immigration crackdown, which has galvanised Trump's supporters but alienated many voters.
Only 37 per cent approve of Trump's handling of immigration, according to an October Reuters/Ipsos poll, down from 50 per cent when he took office.
[[nid:1574072]]
Still, four US immigration officials told Reuters that there have been no signs that the administration will let up. "Nothing is changing, same quotas," said one official.
Representative Don Bacon of Nebraska, an occasional Trump critic who is retiring, told Reuters that Miller "was in denial" as he and other Republican lawmakers tried to warn him before the election that Trump's immigration and tariff policies were driving away voters.
"We said, 'You're going to give us a bad midterm election,' and he rejected it," Bacon said.
The White House said Miller will continue to deliver "historic successes" in his new role, but Bacon said most of his peers in the House view it as "doubling down on a failed strategy."
Miller also has overseen Trump's executive orders, giving him an expansive understanding of the administrative tools available to the president.
Several people interviewed for this story expect the White House to rely on executive orders more extensively rather than working with lawmakers.
"Those on Capitol Hill looking to break away from the Trump administration will know that Stephen Miller is not going to sit idly by and watch that happen," said Republican strategist Ron Bonjean.
As well as the domestic issues he has focused on for most of his career, Miller now will have a greater say in foreign affairs.
Miller opposes prolonging the war with Iran but strongly supports Israel — potentially putting him at odds with a president who has threatened to resume strikes on Iran and announced he will end aid to Tel Aviv.
Miller's elevation also has unnerved corporate lobbyists, who worry he will not be as responsive to their issues as Wiles, who cultivated relationships with top executives.
"This will be a big change," said a senior lobbyist at a Trump-aligned firm.
"Miller is there to focus on political priorities, like immigration and tariffs, stuff Trump cares about, and won't have the same approach as Susie, who understood policies have unintended consequences."
Miller's appointment was met with praise from senior cabinet officials and political supporters, who described him as the fighter they will need in Trump's final stretch.
"I think Donald Trump has found his wartime consigliere," Trump ally Roger Stone said.
* The writers are from Reuters
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Selangor flood evacuees surge past 580, Perak numbers dip
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The number of flood evacuees in Selangor more than doubled, while Perak recorded a slight decline, bringing the total number of victims taking shelter at six temporary relief centres in the two states to 1,002 as of this afternoon.
In Selangor, the number of evacuees rose to 583 people from 163 families as of 3.40pm, compared with 215 people from 55 families this morning.
According to the Welfare Department's InfoBencana portal, all evacuees were housed at four relief centres in Kuala Selangor.
They comprised 326 people from 97 families at SK Dato' Maharaja Lela, 154 people from 36 families at SK Parit Mahang, 77 people from 21 families at Sekolah Agama Batu 8 Ijok, and 26 people from nine families at SK Jaya Setia.
The evacuees comprised 163 adult men, 184 adult women, 127 boys, 97 girls, seven male infants and five female infants, as well as 56 senior citizens and 11 persons with disabilities (PwDs).
In Perak, the number of flood victims in Hilir Perak declined slightly to 419 people from 124 families, compared with 439 people from 130 families this morning.
The State Disaster Management Committee Secretariat said 284 evacuees from 85 families were taking shelter at the Teluk Intan Municipal Council (MPTI) Rest House Hall, while another 135 people from 39 families were at the MPTI Langkap Hall.
Meanwhile, all 26 victims affected by a storm were allowed to return home at noon following the closure of the Manjung Community Hall relief centre.
Two rivers in Perak have also exceeded the danger level, namely Sungai Kinta in Tanjung Tualang, which recorded 12.52 metres, and Sungai Bidor in Changkat Jong, at 3.55 metres.

Title: Lights to go out at Russia's Novaya Gazeta, independent newspaper known for fearless reporting
Article:
MOSCOW: Russian investigative newspaper Novaya Gazeta was winding up its operations on Monday and preparing to quit its central Moscow office after holding its final editorial meeting, bowing to what it said was a campaign of state pressure that had made it impossible to carry on reporting.
The paper, founded by the last Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev with money from his 1990 Nobel Peace Prize, had kept going until now despite a sharp tightening of censorship after Russia launched its full-scale war in Ukraine in 2022.
But it announced late last month that it would have to close after it was designated a "foreign agent" and banks stopped processing reader donations on which it relied for its financial survival.
Its offices and the home of its editor were searched, and another senior journalist is under house arrest awaiting trial.
"The most awful thing is that we who lead editorial teams cannot protect our journalists," former editor in chief Dmitry Muratov told an audience in London last month.
[[nid:1574052]]
Muratov shared the 2021 Nobel Peace Prize, dedicating it to six slain colleagues, including investigative journalist Anna Politkovskaya, who wrote about Russia's wars in the restive Chechnya region.
The Kremlin - which accuses foreign intelligence services of trying to stir discontent in Russian society - has said previously that some censorship is necessary at a time when Russia is locked in what it calls an existential struggle with the West over Ukraine.
Some hardliner war bloggers have accused Novaya Gazeta of systematically promoting an anti-Russian narrative, an allegation it has repeatedly dismissed as false.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov played down the outlet's closure on Monday, saying it was part of what he called "a standard rotational process" in which some media closed only to have their places taken by newcomers in what he said was a fiercely competitive media environment.
A long article on Novaya Gazeta's  website described its journalists' operation to pack up and vacate their premises.
It quoted a senior journalist, Irina Vorobyova, as saying its spirit would survive like a "good virus" - "Not even a nuclear explosion could destroy it. It will continue in everyone who was part of it."

Title: [UPDATED] Anwar announces RM2,500 additional aid for Selangor flood-hit households
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Each eligible household affected by floods in Selangor will receive RM2,500 in special additional cash assistance, with payments expected to begin tomorrow.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced the assistance in a statement issued by the Prime Minister's Office.
The aid is intended to help households replace necessities damaged or destroyed by the floods.
"The implementation mechanism and eligibility criteria will be announced by the implementing agency," the statement said.
It added that Anwar had also directed that flood mitigation projects be expedited to address recurring floods.
Flood evacuees in Selangor rose to 583 people from 163 families as of 3.40pm, compared with 215 people from 55 families in the morning.
Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said on Friday that the recent floods were caused by unusually heavy rainfall.
He said the state was pursuing both
long-term flood mitigation projects
and immediate measures, but it was unrealistic to expect floods to disappear overnight.
The 2026/2027 northeast monsoon began on Oct 27 and is expected to last until March next year.
Malaysian Meteorological Department director-general Dr Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip said three to five episodes of
continuous heavy rain
were expected between November and January, potentially triggering floods in low-lying areas and riverine communities.
The department's National Weather and Earthquake Operations Centre senior director Maqrun Fadzli Mohd Fahmi said the risk of major floods would increase if prolonged heavy rain coincided with
high tides.
In August, the Selangor and federal governments agreed on five measures to mitigate flooding in the Klang Valley following a meeting between Amirudin and Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh.
The measures include assessing the capacity of
Batu Dam and Klang Gates Dam,
identifying potential sites for new flood retention ponds, and coordinating river dredging and desilting works.

Title: Tears and joy as Ukrainian couple divided by occupation meet again
Article:
LARYSA Ryndova hurried to see her husband as if they were going out on a first date — makeup on and perfume spritzed in the car.
It was the first time she had laid eyes on 68-year-old Serhiy in 4-1/2 years — time he had spent trapped with others in the Russian-held town of Oleshky in southern Ukraine.
"I can't believe you are here," Larysa, 72, kept repeating, her mascara smudged with tears after they embraced outside a hospital in Kyiv.
"Honestly, I can't believe it myself," Serhiy replied.
They last saw each other in 2022 when Larysa fled to England to live with their son, three months into the occupation following Russia's all-out invasion of Ukraine.
Serhiy stayed to look after the family home, ending up stuck in the town peppered with Russian-laid landmines and facing a mounting humanitarian crisis.
"We hoped for better. Turned out, it got 'better'," he said sarcastically.
Oleshky's residents described living through constant drone attacks and without power and heating. Things got even worse this spring, when food deliveries stopped.
Serhiy got out on October 30 with hundreds of other residents, evacuated during a ceasefire that US first lady Melania Trump was involved in brokering, with the additional involvement of Pope Leo.
For all the joy of seeing Larysa — and the prospect of being reunited with his three children and six grandchildren — he had found his escape from Oleshky a devastating wrench.
"Your heart is torn apart at the thought of leaving everything behind. How can you? Your home, your family, the cemetery — all your relatives are there," he said.
"How will you ever visit their graves, keep them cared for?"
As Oleshky's evacuees were moved by buses and planes through occupied land, Russia and Belarus, Larysa set out on her own 2,000-km journey to meet Serhiy and bring him back with her to Britain.
"How haggard he looks," she said when she saw the first pictures of her husband crossing into Ukraine. "It's hard to recognise him."
[[nid:1574094]]
Serhiy called Oleshky a "zone of death" where life under occupation could depend on the mood of an individual Russian soldier.
He survived on humanitarian aid that he had stockpiled during the occupation — noodles, grains, sometimes canned meat and fish. He tried frying up flatbreads with flour stored before the war, riddled with weevils.
"Sometime around April (this year), the people who used to bring us food died — two men. After that, all food deliveries stopped completely. There was nothing," Serhiy said over a cup of coffee in a Kyiv cafe.
Locals shared what they had. Some risked the dangerous 20-km journey on foot or bicycle to Radensk for supplies. Rare provisions were sold at severely inflated prices.
The local hospital ran out of supplies. Bodies were stacked up in the morgue, as forensic experts refused to risk the journey to the town to perform autopsies.
"Bodies are just lying there. Everything is leaking. When my neighbour died, I carried his body in there, and the smell was absolutely horrific," Serhiy said. "God forbid!"
Another neighbour asked him to bury her in her own courtyard if she ever got killed.
Serhiy said he probably would not have left the town himself had it not been for the evacuation. Landmines were laid out on all the roads and even in the town.
"They (Russian troops) had their own objective, as I understand it: to mine everything so they could keep everything under control," he added.
"A lot of people were killed in Oleshky. Someone would go out to pick a cherry plum and get blown up. Someone else would pick up a mushroom or a nut and step on a landmine."
Serhiy said Russian troops "had done a great job of cleaning up" to put on a show before the organised evacuations began. He didn't see a single burnt-out car on the way.
He said he felt sure he could have survived another winter, despite the ordeal of occupation and food shortages.
Larysa rolled her eyes, still wet with tears.
"I'll fatten him up with borscht and varenyky (dumplings)," she said.
* The writer is from Reuters
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka polls: EC makes final preparations for early voting
Article:
MELAKA: Preparations are in full swing at early voting centres across the state ahead of tomorrow's early voting for the 16th Melaka election.
At SK Kem Terendak 2, Election Commission (EC) personnel were seen making final arrangements from about 2pm today.
They set up voting compartments, arranged tables according to the EC's prescribed layout and put up banners, notices and posters providing guidance to voters.
Military personnel also erected several canopies outside the school compound to provide waiting areas for voters and members of the media.
A total of 12,531 early voters are expected to cast their ballots tomorrow at 31 early voting centres, which will open from 8am.

Title: Johari shows kampung spirit in checkers match with Duyong residents
Article:
MELAKA: Umno vice-president Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani took a break from the campaign trail today to join residents of Kampung Bukit Godek, Semabok, for a friendly game of checkers, locally known as dam haji.
The light-hearted match saw Johari displaying his skills at the traditional board game, even beating a local resident.
He was visiting the village with Barisan Nasional Duyong candidate Datuk Mohd Noor Helmy Abdul Halem as part of the coalition's campaign for the Melaka state election.
Helmy said the impromptu match gave residents a glimpse of Johari's down-to-earth personality and his kampung roots.
"Datuk Johari came here and played dam haji with the villagers. He even won the match.
"It showed his true personality, the kampung side of him from his younger days," he said.
Earlier today, Johari attended a briefing with BN election machinery for the Ayer Molek and Pengkalan Batu constituencies.
Also present were BN's Ayer Molek candidate Datuk Mohd Ridhwan Mohd Ali and Pengkalan Batu candidate Siti Aisyah Mahmood.
Helmy is defending the Duyong seat against Pakatan Harapan's Poo Long Suan.
In the 2021 Melaka state election, Helmy won the seat with 4,684 votes, securing a slim majority of 200.

Title: Melaka polls: Paya Rumput Indian community wants better-paying jobs, temple assistance
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 9 — Competitively paid job opportunities and assistance for the upkeep of places of worship are among the key issues raised by the Indian community in the Paya Rumput state constituency, which they hope will receive attention from the candidates elected during the Melaka state election.
Mechanical engineer Sathesh Kumaar A/L Gunasegaran, 24, said graduate employability and competitive salaries were important benchmarks in determining who should be elected to serve the residents of Paya Rumput.
He said the state government and the incoming elected representative should formulate initiatives to narrow the salary gap in Melaka and bring it closer to the level offered in states such as Johor, in order to prevent the migration of local talent.
“Among the issues I can highlight for the younger generation is, first and foremost, the unemployment rate. Perhaps Melaka is not on par with states such as Johor in terms of how they have brought about changes in salaries and job opportunities.
“Besides that, I also hope candidates can introduce activities or programmes that benefit school students and help improve their education and living standards,” he told Bernama.
K Selvie a/p Kannon, 58, said the Indian community in the constituency appreciated federal government assistance such as the Rahmah Cash Contribution (STR), Rahmah Basic Contribution (SARA) and other forms of aid, but also hoped that the needs of places of worship would be addressed. — Bernama pic
Sharing similar views, electrical and electronic engineering graduate Kuhan, 24, who goes by a single name, said Gen Z youths like him faced difficulties entering the job market if existing industrial areas in Paya Rumput were not fully utilised.
“It’s really not easy to find a job. Even as a fresh graduate, I’m actually struggling to get one. But honestly, I feel that if we vote for the right party that can establish a proper foundation for our country, we as Gen Z can lead the country and have a better future with a stronger foundation,” he said.
Apart from employment and salary issues, the Indian community in Paya Rumput also hopes that the welfare of its religious institutions, particularly places of worship, will receive attention from the constituency’s incoming elected representative.
Sharing similar views, electrical and electronic engineering graduate Kuhan, 24, said Gen Z youths like him faced difficulties entering the job market if existing industrial areas in Paya Rumput were not fully utilised. — Bernama pic
K Selvie a/p Kannon, 58, said the Indian community in the constituency appreciated federal government assistance such as the Rahmah Cash Contribution (STR), Rahmah Basic Contribution (SARA) and other forms of aid, but also hoped that the needs of places of worship would be addressed.
The mother of five hopes that the elected representative for Paya Rumput will help ease the financial burden of relocating a temple from its former site to a new site purchased by the community.
“This assistance is not for personal gain, but for the benefit of the younger generation and our grandchildren and future generations, so that they can worship in comfort and safety,” she said.
The Election Commission has set November 14 as polling day for the Melaka state election, while early voting will take place on November 10.

Title: Melaka polls: Anwar urges military, police voters to back Pakatan candidates
Article:
