Title: Kajang woman arrested over alleged vandalism of electrical panel with ‘Allah’ inscription, cross
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 9 — A local woman in her 40s has been arrested on suspicion of vandalising an electrical control panel by painting the word “Allah” and a cross on it at the roadside in Taman Sutera in Kajang.
Kajang district police chief Assistant Commissioner Naazron Abdul Yusof said the woman was detained by a team from the district police headquarters' Criminal Investigation Division at about 2.15pm today, Kosmo! Online reported.
He said the arrest followed a police report lodged at 12.16pm yesterday over a video circulating on social media that allegedly showed the woman carrying out the act.
“Following the report, police managed to arrest a local woman in her 40s to assist in investigations.
“Several items were also seized, including red paint and clothing believed to be linked to the incident,” he said in a statement today.
Naazron said investigations were ongoing to establish the motive, including recording witness statements and examining the viral video.
He said the case was being investigated under Section 298 of the Penal Code for deliberately wounding the religious feelings of others, an offence punishable by up to one year in prison, a fine, or both.
“Investigations are also being conducted under Section 427 of the Penal Code and Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998,” he said.
He urged members of the public with information about the incident to assist investigations by contacting investigating officer Inspector Muhammad Nazirulzahin Mohd Hashim at 017-8881475.
He stressed that firm action would be taken against anyone found to have committed an offence under existing laws.
Earlier, a video circulating on social media showed a woman suspected of using red paint to draw the word “Allah and a cross on an electrical control panel at the roadside in Taman Sutera, Kajang.
The incident drew police attention and led to the woman’s arrest to assist in investigations.

Title: Health Ministry deploys 387 personnel in 85 teams for monsoon flood response
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Nov 9 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) has prepared 85 Emergency Medical Teams comprising 387 personnel to respond to possible flooding during the 2026/2027 North-east Monsoon (MTL).
In a statement today, the ministry said these comprised 36 Rapid Assessment and Health Rapid Response Teams, 34 Medical Rapid Response Teams and 15 Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) teams.
“The teams will be mobilised as required to conduct health risk assessments, provide medical services and emergency treatment, carry out surveillance and control of infectious diseases, as well as provide mental health and psychosocial support to flood victims,” it said.
The ministry has also made available 128 vehicles to support personnel mobilisation and field operations, while flood-related medicine supplies at warehouses operated by concessionaire suppliers remain stable, with stocks estimated to last between one and three months.
Through the National Crisis Preparedness and Response Centre (CPRC), State Health Departments, District Health Offices and healthcare facilities nationwide, the ministry has also stepped up preparedness to ensure continued healthcare services, particularly in flood-prone areas.
The National CPRC has been in Alert Mode since October 27, with continuous monitoring of flood situations, healthcare facility preparedness and coordination of response measures with State Health Departments and relevant agencies.
The ministry said healthcare facilities at risk of flooding had also been identified, together with alternative facilities in the event of operational disruptions. Plans were also in place for the early transfer of high-risk patients, including pregnant women and those requiring haemodialysis.
As of 6am today, floods had been reported in Selangor and Perak, affecting 987 people from 283 families, who were housed at seven active temporary relief centres (PPS).
Meanwhile, the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) expects three to five monsoon surges during the North-east Monsoon, which could bring heavy rain, particularly to the eastern and southern parts of Peninsular Malaysia, eastern Sabah, and western and southern Sarawak.
The ministry said the risk of flooding could increase if prolonged rain coincided with high tides.
At relief centres, the ministry provides health assessments, infectious disease monitoring, environmental hygiene inspections, food and water safety checks, vector control, as well as mental health and psychosocial support.
These measures are aimed at reducing the risk of flood-related illnesses, including diarrhoea, food poisoning, leptospirosis and respiratory tract infections.
The ministry also advised the public to use clean and safe drinking water, consume properly cooked food and avoid food contaminated by floodwaters.
People were also advised to maintain personal and environmental hygiene, wash their hands frequently with clean water and soap, and avoid direct contact with potentially contaminated floodwaters.
“Those experiencing symptoms such as fever, diarrhoea, vomiting and muscle pain after exposure to floodwaters are advised to seek immediate medical examination and treatment at healthcare facilities,” the ministry said.
The ministry also reminded patients with chronic illnesses, senior citizens, pregnant women and children to ensure continuity of treatment and adequate medication supplies in the event they need to move to relief centres. — Bernama

Title: Kelantan deploys almost 60 psychological support workers to help flood victims cope with trauma
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Nov 9 — A total of 59 members of the Psychological Support Team (PST) from various agencies, including the Ministry of Health and the Ministry of Education, will be deployed to temporary evacuation centres (PPS) in Kelantan to help address the trauma and emotional stress of flood victims throughout the Northeast Monsoon (MTL) 2026/2027.
Kelantan Department of Social Welfare (JKM) director Che Samsuzuki Che Noh said that in addition to providing psychological support, the team will also organise various activities to help reduce the emotional stress of the victims while they are at the PPS.
He said that the Kelantan JKM also mobilised 400 officers and staff, 13 counselling officers, and 327 volunteers to ensure the smooth operation of disaster management and aid distribution.
In this regard, he encourages those interested in becoming volunteers to register with the JKM early to facilitate the coordination of assistance during disasters.
In another development, Che Samsuzuki urged the public to register early through the MyIBJKM application to facilitate the process when they are relocated to the PPS.
He said the information that needs to be completed in the application includes details of the Head of Household (KIR), family members, place of residence, and children's schools to enable victim profiling to be done earlier.
“This information is important for facilitating data management and preventing the duplication of information. Once registration is completed, the relevant data will be channelled directly to the National Disaster Management Agency, thereby helping to expedite the provision of assistance, including the Bantuan Wang Ihsan (BWI),” he said.
He added that early registration also helps expedite the BWI payment process, including after the PPS is closed.
So far, a total of 79,455 KIR with a total of 135,616 household members have been recorded in the system, while 69,101 KIR have registered through the MyIBJKM application in its second year of implementation.
He also urged the district-level JKM to intensify the campaign for the application registration during disaster management simulations to avoid congestion and delays in the registration process during floods. — Bernama

Title: Melaka polls: 12,531 military, police personnel and spouses to cast early ballots tomorrow
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 9 — Some 12,531 eligible early voters in the 16th Melaka State Election will cast their ballots across 31 gazetted early polling centres statewide tomorrow.
They comprise 9,769 military personnel and their spouses, and 2,762 police personnel.
All polling centres will open at 8am tomorrow and close in stages between 12pm and 6pm, depending on the location and the number of registered electors.
Several centres with smaller electorates, including the Masjid Tanah Police Station for the Lendu state constituency and the Gadek Police Station for the Gadek state constituency, are scheduled to close as early as noon.
Polling centres at the Melaka Contingent Police Headquarters, the Alor Gajah District Police Headquarters, and SK Kem Terendak 1 are scheduled to close at 6pm.
Overall, 687,697 electors are eligible to vote in the state election.
The election sees Pakatan Harapan fielding candidates in 24 state seats, followed by Barisan Nasional (23), Parti Bersama Malaysia (16), Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (seven), Perikatan Nasional (five), Parti Pribumi Perkasa Malaysia (one), and three Independents.
In the 2021 Melaka State Election, Barisan Nasional won 21 seats to form the state government, while Pakatan Harapan won five seats and Perikatan Nasional two.
The Election Commission has set polling day for November 14.
For the latest updates on the election, visit
https://election.bernama.com/pm/melaka/2026/
. — Bernama

Title: ECRL enters final trial run ahead of Dec 12 passenger service launch
Article:
GOMBAK, Nov 9 — Malaysia Rail Link Sdn Bhd (MRL) is conducting trial operations for the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) as part of the final preparations ahead of the planned launch of commercial passenger services on December 12, 2026.
MRL said in a statement that the trial operations programme is intended to assess operational readiness, service efficiency, station management and the passenger experience under actual operating conditions, Kosmo! Online reported.
Running from November 7 to December 2, 2026, the programme covers journeys between Gombak and Kota Bharu in both directions, and includes express and transit services.

Title: Lexi’s final mission: Sabah rescue dog dies after helping find missing man following nine years of service
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Nov 9 — A Sabah Fire and Rescue Department search dog died a day after completing its final search-and-rescue mission, bringing nearly nine years of service with the department’s K9 unit to an end.
The 10-year-old Labrador Retriever, named Lexi, was found dead in its kennel at 6.15am last Friday, according to a report by
Harian Metro
.
Lexi had taken part in a search operation for a missing person in Kampung Pulutan Membawang, Menggatal, on November 5, making it the dog’s final assignment with the rescue team.
Sabah Fire and Rescue Department K9 unit chief Calvin Joe Jeafery said Lexi had been accompanied by its handler, fireman Arthur Anderson Walter, during the operation.
After returning to the station, Lexi was bathed and fed as part of its usual care routine, with Calvin saying the dog finished its food and showed no change in behaviour.
However, personnel found it unresponsive when they called its name during a routine kennel inspection the following morning, and further checks confirmed that it had died.
Calvin said Lexi had a medical history that included stage-two heart disease and a growth on its gums.
The dog had been under veterinary supervision and received treatment including antibiotics, gastric medication and anti-inflammatory drugs.
Its cause of death has yet to be established, pending a post-mortem report from the Sabah Veterinary Services Department, he said.
During its service, Lexi was trained in wilderness search-and-rescue operations, specialising in locating missing people in forests and other challenging terrain.
The dog joined the Sabah K9 unit after being acquired from the United Kingdom in 2017, and its final operation in Menggatal marked the close of a career spanning almost nine years.

Title: Three killed by lightning strike in Bandar Baru Salak Tinggi, police confirm
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 9 — Three people were killed after being struck by lightning in an incident in Bandar Baru Salak Tinggi in Sepang this afternoon.
Sepang District Police Chief Assistant Commissioner Norhizam Bahaman confirmed the incident when contacted, Kosmo! Online reported.
“Yes,” he said briefly when contacted to confirm the incident.
The incident is believed to have occurred at a public field near Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan Seri Sepang.
Earlier, several video clips showing three bodies covered with batik cloths lying under a tree went viral on social media.
The three victims were believed to have been at the location after the car they were travelling in broke down.
The victims were taken to Sultan Idris Shah Hospital in Serdang for further action.

Title: Repeat drug-positive driver arrested after another crash in Kuala Pilah
Article:
KUALA PILAH, Nov 9 — A male driver who was previously involved in an accident involving five vehicles and tested positive for drugs was again involved in an accident along Jalan Seremban-Kuala Pilah, near Tanjong Ipoh town, here, last Saturday.
Kuala Pilah District Police Chief Supt Muhamad Mustafah Hussin said the accident at about 2.45pm was believed to have occurred when a Toyota Vios driven by the suspect, travelling from Seremban towards Bahau, rammed into the rear of a Nissan Grand Livina multi-purpose vehicle (MPV).
He said the impact caused the Nissan Grand Livina to skid forward before hitting a Proton Wira.
“Police urine screening found substances suspected to be MDMA and Eramin 5. The suspect was arrested and taken to the Kuala Pilah District Police Headquarters for further investigation,” he said in a statement today.
Muhamad Mustafah said the 39-year-old suspect had previously been charged under Section 44(1A) of the Road Transport Act 1987 for driving under the influence of drugs, resulting in injuries to other road users.
He said no injuries were reported among the drivers involved in the accident, although all three vehicles sustained damage. — Bernama

Title: Paya Terubong landslide: Penang to decide developer’s fate after DOSH probe
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Nov 9 — Any action against the developer involved in the landslide at Taman Seri Rambai, Paya Terubong, here, which claimed the life of a doctor on October 25, will hinge on the findings of an investigation by the Department of Occupational Safety and Health (DOSH).
Penang Local Government and Town and Country Planning Committee chairman H’ng Mooi Lye said the state government would await the outcome of DOSH’s investigation before deciding on further action.
“We will await DOSH’s findings,” he told Bernama when contacted to comment on possible action against the project developer.
On mitigation works at the affected site, he said consulting engineers had informed authorities at a recent coordination meeting that the initial work would focus on Zones A and B, with completion expected to take between four and five months.
However, the developer must first submit Pre-Construction Information (PCI) documents to DOSH for assessment before mitigation works can begin.
H’ng said the Penang Island City Council (MBPP) had no objection to the proposed mitigation measures, subject to DOSH’s final approval.
In the incident, which occurred at 8.36am on Oct 25, 73-year-old Dr Wong Kar Lin died after being buried in a landslide that affected his home, while his wife, Chang Mei Nuo, 68, and his mother-in-law, Wong Poh Lim (in her 80s), managed to escape.
The state government had held the developer and landowner of a condominium and road project responsible for the tragedy, stressing that they were accountable for safety and mitigation measures at the project site.
Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow was also reported to have warned of possible legal consequences, while emphasising that the landslide occurred on the developer’s land.
A coordination meeting chaired by H’ng was held on November 2 to review the investigation into the incident and determine whether further measures were necessary to address safety issues in the area. — Bernama

Title: Nacsa records 5,110 cyber incidents in Malaysia from January to September
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 9 — The National Cyber Security Agency (Nacsa) recorded 5,110 cybersecurity incidents from January to September this year, compared with 5,837 incidents last year.
Nacsa chief executive Dr Megat Zuhairy Megat Tajuddin said the higher number of incidents recorded last year was largely driven by intrusion attempts and potential attacks, which were detected at an early stage.
He said Nacsa’s National Cyber Coordination and Command Centre (NC4) had also issued nine alerts and advisories in October and November this year, concerning security vulnerabilities affecting National Critical Information Infrastructure (NCII) entities and government agencies.
“It is important to understand that not all cybersecurity incidents have the same impact, and Nacsa’s main focus is on incidents which have the potential to disrupt the country’s essential services,” he told Bernama here today.
He said the cybersecurity incidents recorded included a ransomware attack on Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd in March 2025, which caused disruptions at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) for more than 10 hours.
Commenting on the viral Live Map & Ranking display, which placed Malaysia among the countries receiving the highest number of cyber attacks, Megat Zuhairy said the figures were based on monitoring through specific cyber security products and platforms, widely used by organisations in Malaysia.
“The sensors installed enable proactive monitoring of detected cyber activities and traffic, providing an overview based on data from these sources.
“Additionally, Malaysia is one of the key data centre hubs globally, and this position means that a large volume of international internet traffic passes through the country, either as a target of cyber attacks, or as a transit route to other destinations,” he said.
Megat Zuhairy said the display did not reflect the overall cyber security situation of a country, as a comprehensive assessment would need to take into account various other factors and data sources.
These include actual cyber security incidents, as detected activities or attempted attacks do not necessarily mean that an organisation has experienced an incident or system breach.
He said there was currently no specific global ranking or report comparing countries, based on actual cyber attack incidents. However, based on the National Cyber Threat Level (NCTL) assessment, Malaysia’s cyber threat level remained moderate, while the country was placed in Tier 1 under the Global Cybersecurity Index (GCI).
He added that Malaysia was also preparing for the transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC), to address developments in quantum computing technology.
Megat Zuhairy said individuals were also targets of cyber threats, particularly through the hacking of social media, email and online banking accounts.
He reminded the public to understand the difference between account hacking and online scams, so that appropriate action could be taken if they encountered such situations.
“Hacking occurs when another party gains unauthorised access to an account or system. Early warning signs include login notifications from unrecognised devices or locations, passwords being changed without the account owner’s knowledge, or messages being sent from one’s own account without authorisation.
“Scams, on the other hand, occur when victims are deceived into voluntarily handing over money or information, for example, through calls, messages or fake offers,” he said.
Megat Zuhairy also urged users whose accounts had been compromised to immediately change their passwords, activate multi-factor authentication (MFA) and report the matter to the relevant platform provider.
Victims of scams involving money transfers, meanwhile, should contact their banks and the National Scam Response Centre (NSRC) via its hotline at 997.
“Authentic precautionary measures are generally simple and practical, such as activating MFA, keeping devices updated and refraining from sharing personal information.
“The public should also be wary of posts which do not cite clear sources, use an urgent tone, or recommend drastic measures such as withdrawing all their savings,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Toddler goes missing during family outing at Gopeng river, search underway
Article:
IPOH, Nov 9 — A two-year-and-10-month-old boy went missing while enjoying a family outing at Dataran Sungai Jahang, Kampung Jahang, near Gopeng, around midday today.
Perak Fire and Rescue Department Operations Division assistant director Sabarodzi Nor Ahmad said a team from the Gopeng Fire and Rescue Station was dispatched to the scene after receiving a call at 12.06pm.
“The search involved the police, villagers and a nearby tour company, which assisted by providing eight rafting boats.
“By 3.45pm, search teams had extended their initial search to a distance of four kilometres from the location where the victim was reported to have fallen,” he said in a statement.
He said the search area was being expanded this afternoon, with a control post already set up at the scene.
Personnel from the Kampar Fire and Rescue Station were also assisting by monitoring the river downstream near Kampar, he said, adding that the search is still ongoing.
In a separate incident on Pulau Pangkor, a 38-year-old Myanmar worker is feared drowned after reportedly suffering a seizure before falling into the sea.
Sabarodzi said the Pangkor Fire and Rescue Station team was mobilised after receiving a call at 12.54pm.
“The Operations Commander was informed upon arrival that a 38-year-old Myanmar national had suffered a seizure while on a boat docked at the jetty before falling into the sea.
“Efforts to locate the victim are ongoing,” he added. — Bernama

Title: Selangor flood evacuees more than double to 583 as Perak numbers ease
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 9 — The number of flood evacuees in Selangor more than doubled, while Perak recorded a slight improvement, bringing the total number of victims sheltering at six temporary relief centres in the two states to 1,002 as of this afternoon
In Selangor, the number of evacuees rose to 583 people from 163 families as of 3.40pm, compared with 215 people from 55 families this morning.
According to the Social Welfare Department’s (JKM) InfoBencana portal, all the evacuees were housed at four relief centres in Kuala Selangor, namely Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Dato’ Maharaja Lela, which accommodated 326 people from 97 families; SK Parit Mahang (154 people, 36 families); Sekolah Agama Batu 8 Ijok (77 people, 21 families); and SK Jaya Setia (26 people, nine families).
The evacuees comprised 163 adult men, 184 adult women, 127 boys, 97 girls, seven male infants and five female infants, as well as 56 senior citizens and 11 persons with disabilities (PwDs).
In Perak, the number of victims in Hilir Perak declined slightly to 419 people from 124 families, compared with 439 people from 130 families this morning.
The State Disaster Management Committee Secretariat said 284 evacuees from 85 families were taking shelter at the Teluk Intan Municipal Council (MPTI) Rest House Hall, while another 135 people from 39 families were at the MPTI Langkap Hall.
Meanwhile, all 26 victims affected by a storm were allowed to return home at noon following the closure of the Manjung Community Hall relief centre.
Two rivers in Perak have also exceeded the danger level, namely Sungai Kinta in Tanjung Tualang, which recorded a reading of 12.52 metres, and Sungai Bidor in Changkat Jong (3.55 metres). — Bernama

Title: Broke Malaysian overstays in Batam, allegedly robs woman for cash, steals SUV and injures cop before arrest
Article:
BATAM, Nov 9 — A 41-year-old Malaysian man has been arrested in Batam, Indonesia, after allegedly robbing a woman at gunpoint with an airsoft pistol, stealing her car and injuring a police officer while attempting to escape last Friday.
The suspect, from Melaka, allegedly threatened the 48-year-old woman with an airsoft pistol and a knife before fleeing in her Toyota Rush with valuables worth an estimated 292 million rupiah (RM73,000),
Sinar Harian
reported today.
Barelang Police Criminal Investigation Division chief Commissioner Tri Poerbowo said preliminary investigations found that the suspect had entered Indonesia on September 15 for a holiday but overstayed by 10 days after running out of money.
“He then planned a random robbery to obtain money to pay for his return journey to Malaysia,” he was quoted as saying by Indonesian media.
The victim had just paid her vehicle road tax and withdrawn cash from an automated teller machine (ATM) at Harbour Bay before getting into her car.
The suspect allegedly entered the passenger seat unexpectedly, pointed his weapon at her and ordered her to drive to the Bukit Senyum area.
Upon reaching the grounds of a residential development, he forced the victim to transfer money online into his personal bank account.
However, when the woman screamed for help, the suspect panicked, pushed her out of the vehicle and drove off.
A traffic police officer nearby witnessed the incident and gave chase, eventually intercepting the stolen vehicle.
The suspect refused to surrender and pointed his airsoft pistol at the officer before ramming into him, leaving the officer injured.
Police questioning revealed that the suspect had bought the airsoft pistol from an apartment security guard for one million rupiah.
The security guard has also been detained to assist in investigations.
If convicted under Article 365 of Indonesia’s Criminal Code for theft involving violence, the suspect faces a maximum prison sentence of nine years.

Title: Anwar announces RM2,500 flood aid for each eligible household in Selangor
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 9 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today announced a special additional cash aid of RM2,500 for heads of eligible flood-affected households in Selangor, with payments expected to begin tomorrow.
The Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) said in a statement that the assistance is aimed at easing the burden of victims in replacing household essentials damaged or destroyed by the floods, with implementation mechanisms and eligibility criteria to be announced by the executing agency.
“At the same time, the prime minister has also directed that the implementation of flood mitigation projects be expedited to tackle recurring floods,” the statement read.
Meanwhile, speaking to reporters after visiting flood victims in Kuala Selangor, Anwar said the additional RM2,500 aid is intended for families who have endured prolonged displacement and sustained substantial damage from the disaster.
He said the payout is expected to be disbursed starting tomorrow in coordination with the state government to facilitate distribution.
The prime minister said the additional aid, placed under the Prime Minister’s Department’s Implementation Coordination Unit (ICU), is being provided in view of the protracted flood situation and the heavier losses incurred by victims.
He said this assistance is in addition to the RM1,000 Bantuan Wang Ihsan (BWI) distributed under the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma).
“Because some families have been displaced for a prolonged period, the RM1,000 aid is often felt to be insufficient given the heavier damage. Therefore, I am announcing an additional RM2,500 per family in Selangor for those who have faced extended displacement and extensive damage,” he said.
Earlier, Anwar visited flood victims housed at the temporary relief centre at SK Parit Mahang, Jeram, here, which is currently accommodating 154 evacuees from 36 families.
He said the visit was carried out to assess the victims’ situation firsthand, considering the floods that have persisted for several days, along with prevailing weather conditions and high tides.
The prime minister also expressed his appreciation to all federal and state personnel, as well as volunteers, including medical teams, who worked tirelessly to assist flood victims throughout the Deepavali long weekend. — Bernama

Title: ‘Our first priority was grandma’ — families share flood ordeal in Hilir Perak
Article:
TELUK INTAN, Nov 9 — As floodwaters rose around their homes, two families in Hilir Perak faced an urgent challenge — getting their vulnerable loved ones to safety before the situation worsened.
For Mahani Zakaria, 75, protecting her 41-year-old son with disabilities and two orphaned grandchildren mattered far more than saving her belongings when floodwaters began entering her home in Kampung Batu 10, Changkat Jong, several days ago.
Mahani, who has lived in the house since she was 14, said she noticed the water rising at about 7 pm and immediately began moving essential belongings to higher ground.
By 1 am, floodwaters had reached knee level inside her home, prompting her to call the Fire and Rescue Department for assistance.
She and her family were evacuated to the temporary relief centre at the Teluk Intan Municipal Council (MPTI) Rest House Hall at about 2 am.
“I had already packed and moved our important belongings to higher places because I could see the water rising that evening. When it started entering the house, I called the fire department to rescue us,” she told Bernama at the relief centre today.
But the floods are not Mahani’s only concern. The single mother said her ageing house was in poor condition, with a leaking roof, but financial constraints had prevented her from carrying out repairs.
Unemployed, she relies entirely on monthly assistance from the Social Security Organisation (PERKESO) and the Social Welfare Department (JKM) received by her son to support the family.
“I don’t ask for much. I just hope my house can be repaired so I can continue looking after my son and grandchildren,” she said.
For 15-year-old Rizwan Hakimi Faizul, the priority was equally clear when floods struck his family’s home in Ladang Moccis — ensuring the safety of his bedridden grandmother, Maria Abu Bakar, 73, who has been paralysed and unable to speak following a stroke in 2010.
15-year-old Rizwan Hakimi Faizul (right) checks on this grandmother, Maria Abu Bakar, 73, who has been paralysed and unable to speak following a stroke in 2010. — Bernama pic
Rizwan, a GIATMARA student in Negeri Sembilan, said he was asleep at about 8 am when his mother woke him as floodwaters rose to shoulder level around their home.
“Our first priority was our grandmother because she is completely paralysed and cannot speak. We raised her bed using pieces of wood to keep her above the floodwaters. Only after making sure she was safe did we think about our belongings,” he said.
The family spent about 20 to 30 minutes gathering essential items before waiting more than two hours for Civil Defence Force (APM) personnel to arrive.
Maria was subsequently evacuated by ambulance to the MPTI Rest House Hall relief centre.
Rizwan admitted that caring for his grandmother as the water continued to rise was particularly challenging, but her safety remained the family’s overriding concern.
This was the family’s second experience of flooding, having previously been affected on Nov 24 last year.
Seven family members, including Maria, are now staying at the relief centre.
Meanwhile, a total of 424 flood victims from 125 families in Hilir Perak were housed at two relief centres as of noon today.
Hilir Perak police chief ACP Chua Kok Lian said 136 evacuees from 39 families were at the MPTI Langkap Hall, while another 288 from 86 families were at the MPTI Rest House Hall.
He said the Langkap centre opened at 10 am on Nov 6, followed by the Rest House Hall at 10 pm the same day.
The affected areas include Kampung Batu 9 Changkat Jong, Kampung Batu 11½ Jalan Bidor, Kampung Batu 8 Changkat Jong, Kampung Batu 7½ Jalan Changkat Jong (FELCRA), Ladang Moccis and Kampung Batu 10 Changkat Jong.
Chua said the disaster response operations involved APM, JKM, the People’s Volunteer Corps (RELA), the police, the Fire and Rescue Department, the Hilir Perak District and Land Office, and MPTI. — Bernama

Title: Three Malaysians arrested in Mauritius after 76kg cannabis seizure at airport
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 9 — Mauritian authorities arrested three Malaysians after seizing 76.14kg of suspected cannabis from their luggage at Sir Seewoosagur Ramgoolam International Airport.
According to
Free Malaysia Today
(FMT), the suspects, comprising two men aged 30 and 22 and an 18-year-old woman, were detained after arriving in Mauritius on an Emirates flight from Dubai on November 2.
The Mauritius Revenue Authority said the discovery was made after officials stopped the trio for questioning and inspected their checked baggage.
This led to the discovery of 70 black plastic bags that were vacuum-packed containing green leaves believed to be cannabis, the authority said.
One of the suspects was reported to have travelled from Thailand to Dubai before continuing to Mauritius.
According to the authority, the 30-year-old suspect was living and working in Singapore as a security guard, while the other two were from Penang.
The seized drugs were estimated to be worth 114.21 million Mauritian rupees (RM9.87 million).
The arrests are the latest in a string of drug-related cases involving Malaysians in Mauritius.
FMT reported that last month, a 55-year-old Malaysian chef was arrested on suspicion of attempting to smuggle 17.88kg of cannabis after the substance was allegedly found in his luggage.
In a separate case in September, a 76-year-old Malaysian was detained after Mauritian authorities allegedly discovered 6.18kg of cannabis in his baggage.

Title: Return rush begins, major highways congested as Deepavali holiday wraps up
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 9 — Traffic flow on several major highways heading towards the Klang Valley was congested as of 3pm today, as city dwellers began returning home following the Deepavali holiday.
A spokesperson for the Malaysian Highway Authority (LLM) said on the North-South Expressway (PLUS), slow-moving traffic was reported from Sungai Petani Selatan to Bertam, Sungai Dua to Juru Autocity, Kuala Kangsar to the Meru Tunnel, Simpang Pulai to Gopeng, and Gopeng to Bidor.
“Meanwhile, for the southern route, congestion is occurring from Kulai to Simpang Renggam, Ayer Keroh to Simpang Ampat, Pedas Linggi to Port Dickson, Bandar Ainsdale to Nilai Utara, Southville City to Kajang, and from Sungai Besi towards the city centre,” the spokesperson told Bernama today.
Additionally, traffic moving from the East Coast towards the capital is also congested, specifically along the stretches from Lanchang to the Karak Toll Plaza, Bentong to Lentang, and Genting Sempah to the Gombak Toll Plaza.
The spokesperson advised motorists to drive cautiously, as heavy rain in several locations is further contributing to the slow traffic flow.
The public can obtain the latest traffic updates by contacting the LLM toll-free hotline at 1800-88-7752. — Bernama

Title: Melaka polls: Pakatan pledges grants for women traders, proposes more childcare centres, says Adly Zahari
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 9 — Special grants for women traders and a proposal to increase the number of government-operated childcare centres are among Pakatan Harapan’s (PH) offers if it is given the mandate to govern Melaka in the 16th state election.
Melaka PH chairman Adly Zahari said the grants were aimed at strengthening household incomes in the state.
He said the grants, offered under the Women Empowerment aspiration in the ‘Melaka Rumah Kita’ manifesto, would also cater to the actual needs of traders, including purchasing equipment, increasing stock and expanding production capacity.
He said opportunities to help generate household income would be difficult to fully utilise if parents did not have access to suitable childcare services, particularly those working shifts.
“Location, affordability, operating hours and safety must be the main considerations to ensure these facilities suit parents’ routines, including those working shifts,” he said at a daily press conference at the PH Main Operations Room in Bukit Baru here today.
Elaborating, Adly, who is also the PH candidate for the Bukit Katil seat, said PH wanted to help women running small businesses and small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) expand their businesses according to their respective needs.
“This support must take into account actual needs, such as purchasing equipment, increasing stock and boosting production capacity.
“The selection of recipients, meanwhile, should be based on eligibility and reasonable plans for utilising the funds, accompanied by guidance on cost management and marketing,” he said.
He said meetings with members of the public during the campaign had revealed that many small-scale entrepreneurs still needed guidance on marketing their products online and making use of available media platforms.
The former Melaka Chief Minister said marketing training and technical support were important for women entrepreneurs in the SME sector to build stronger businesses, retain customers and contribute to their families’ financial stability.
“Women make up a significant proportion of voters in Melaka, and PH wants to ensure that women in business have access to childcare and reliable support resources so that they can continue contributing to the country,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Minister says Puspal, Jakim verifying claims of religious sensitivity breach at The Weeknd concert
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 9 — Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Senator Dr Zulkifli Hasan has said that firm action will be taken if The Weeknd’s concert in Bukit Jalil is found to have breached religious sensitivities.
In a Facebook post today, Zulkifli stressed that Islam strictly prohibits any form of worship of anything other than Allah.
“All parties must ensure that artistic performances do not cause confusion related to faith, morals, and religious sensitivities in Malaysia,” he said.
He said the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs), through the Jakim Research Division, is in close contact with the secretariat of the Central Agencies Committee for the Application of Filming and Performance by Foreign Artists (Puspal).
This is to verify the validity of claims and compliance with the conditions of The Weeknd’s concert at Bukit Jalil, he said.
“Firm action based on law and verified facts will be taken to ensure every performance by local and foreign artists always preserves religious sensitivities, culture, and public order,” he said.

Title: Woman jailed three months, fined RM5,000 for dumping baby with missing head, arm in Kuala Berang drain
Article:
KUALA BERANG, Nov 9 — A restaurant worker was sentenced to three months’ jail and fined RM5,000 by the Magistrate’s Court here today after pleading guilty to concealing the birth of her child by dumping the infant’s body in a drain.
Magistrate Nur Athirah Hashim also ordered the accused, Nur Ain Adilin Mohd Rofiza, 23, to serve an additional five months in jail if she failed to pay the fine.
She was charged with concealing the birth of her child by disposing of the infant’s body in a drain at Perumahan Awam Kos Rendah, Padang Setengge, here at 10pm on October 15.
The charge was framed under Section 318 of the Penal Code, which provides for a maximum jail term of two years or a fine or both upon conviction.
Earlier, lawyer Nor Aziah Bunawan from the National Legal Aid Foundation (YBGK) urged the court to impose a minimum sentence in the form of a fine, saying the accused was still young and had acted out of panic.
“The accused’s guilty plea has saved the court and prosecution time. She has also expressed remorse for her actions and pledged not to repeat the offence,” she said.
However, Deputy Public Prosecutor Nur Anith Nabilah Rusli urged the court to impose a jail term, citing humanitarian considerations as the case involved the accused’s own child and stressing the need for a sentence that would serve as a deterrent to others.
Earlier, Hulu Terengganu district police chief Supt Sharudin Abdul Wahab said an infant’s body, with its head and one arm missing, was found in a drain in a residential area in Kampung Padang Setengge on October 16.
He said the post-mortem examination confirmed that the infant was full-term. — Bernama

Title: Melaka polls: Pakatan’s Adly Zahari urges civil servants to consider govt’s efforts in raising their pay
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 9 — The various initiatives and policies implemented by the federal government for civil servants should be taken into consideration by the 12,531 security personnel and their spouses who will be casting their early votes in the 16th Melaka state election tomorrow.
Melaka Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman Adly Zahari said these initiatives include a 15 per cent salary increase for civil servants through the implementation of the Public Service Remuneration System (SSPA), in addition to the government’s efforts to strengthen the national economy.
“It is clear that the government under the Prime Minister (Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim) has fulfilled long-standing promises, such as the salary increase.
“Malaysia has also successfully overcome economic constraints previously one of the greatest challenges the nation faced following the Covid-19 pandemic at a time when several other countries, including those in this region, are still grappling with economic difficulties,” he said during a daily press conference at the Pakatan Harapan (PH) Main Operations Room in Bukit Baru here today.
Adly, who is also the PH candidate for the Bukit Katil state constituency, said beyond economic performance and Malaysia’s international standing, he hopes civil servants will also take into account the efforts to strengthen integrity, transparency, and national governance when casting their votes tomorrow.
Elaborating further, Adly, the former Chief Minister of Melaka noted that PH has taken steps to engage with early voters, explaining the coalition’s direction as well as the federal government’s policies and initiatives that benefit them and their families.
The Election Commission (EC) has designated tomorrow as the early voting day for the 16th Melaka state election, with November 14 set as the official polling day.

. — Bernama

Title: Police say pistol-wielding man in viral Kuala Lumpur chase was conducting anti-drug operation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 9 — The man seen holding what appeared to be a pistol while pursuing a car in a viral video along Jalan Sultan Salahuddin here is believed to be a police officer involved in a special anti-drug operation on Saturday.
According to
Berita Harian
(BH), Dang Wangi district police chief Assistant Commissioner Ahmad Azwan Amin Nordin said the incident occurred at about 6.30pm when a team from the Dang Wangi District Police Headquarters Narcotics Criminal Investigation Division spotted a suspicious black Honda Accord.
He said officers approached the vehicle for inspection, but the driver allegedly sped off recklessly and collided with a blue Honda City in an attempt to escape.
Police managed to track down the vehicle again at about 6.40pm at the Jalan Sultan Salahuddin intersection before giving chase. Two men then exited the Honda Accord and fled the scene.
Ahmad Azwan told BH an initial inspection of the vehicle did not uncover any illegal items, adding that police were currently tracking down the two men to assist with further investigations.
Earlier, a one-minute and 13-second video uploaded on Threads showed traffic stopped at an intersection while the lights were red.
The footage showed a man holding an object resembling a pistol while pursuing a vehicle through the intersection.
The incident drew widespread attention on social media, with users questioning the man’s actions.
Police detected the viral video yesterday and confirmed that the incident had taken place the day before.
Anyone with information about the case is urged to contact the Kuala Lumpur Police Hotline at 03-2146 0522 or 03-2146 0585, the Dang Wangi District Police Headquarters Control Centre at 03-2600 2222, or the nearest police station.

Title: Melaka polls: Mandarin fluency a bonus for Pakatan’s Farzana in reaching Kelebang Chinese voters
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 9 — The ability to speak Mandarin gives Pakatan Harapan (PH) candidate for the Kelebang state constituency Farzana Hayani Mohd Nasir an advantage in reaching Chinese voters, particularly the elderly.
Her presence in Pokok Mangga here to campaign for the 16th Melaka State Election attracted the attention of 63-year-old senior citizen Fang Kong Goon, who praised the young Malay candidate for her friendliness in engaging with the Chinese community.
“Being able to speak Mandarin makes it easier for Farzana to introduce herself to the Chinese community, especially the elderly, while building closer ties with them.
“At the same time, using Mandarin when campaigning among the Chinese community facilitates the delivery of information, including about her manifesto and aspirations should she become their elected representative,” the trader told Bernama when met at Geok Hu Keng Temple here.
The temple caretaker, Ku Chin Siew, 70, said Farzana Hayani, affectionately known as Nana by the local community, was no stranger in the area as she frequently visited and engaged with the Chinese community.
“I like seeing Malays who can speak Chinese. It makes things easier because I am not very fluent in Malay myself. It is good to see a young Malay candidate who can speak Chinese,” she said.
Meanwhile, Farzana Hayani, 26, said she was very close to the Chinese community as she had attended Ying Chye Chinese National-type Primary School in Bukit Rambai and Melaka Chinese High School, besides taking Mandarin as a subject in the Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) examination.
The Kelebang-born candidate also acknowledged that her Mandarin fluency had greatly helped her engage with the Chinese community during campaigning, making them feel more comfortable interacting with her.
“Many Chinese people whom I meet during campaigning, especially at eateries and during walkabouts, are surprised when they hear me speaking Mandarin, and conversations about politics become more relaxed.
“Alhamdulillah, this is an advantage for me, and most of the responses I have received from the Chinese community in Kelebang have been positive. I hope this will be reflected in the ballot papers later,” she said.
Farzana Hayani is facing a four-cornered contest against Datuk Lim Ban Hong (Barisan Nasional), Datuk Seri Mohamad Ali Mohamad (Bersatu) and Young Jie Yu (Bersama).
The Election Commission has set November 14 as polling day for the Melaka state election, with early voting on November 10.

Title: Ab Rauf: Melaka flood efforts to continue until issue resolved, RM432m allocated for Sungai Baru Hilir project
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 9 — The Melaka state government will continue its efforts to address flooding issues throughout the state until the root causes are identified and resolved, said Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh.
He said a phased approach tailored to specific areas will continue to be implemented, taking into account various factors, including inadequate drainage systems and natural phenomena.
“As long as the flooding issue remains unresolved, I will not cease serving the people. We will identify the root causes of these floods.
“It is possible that we lack a well-organised and properly planned drainage system, it could also be due to natural phenomena that we must take into account,” he told Bernama.
Ab Rauf said the state government is managing flood mitigation projects with funding support from the federal government including a new mitigation project at Sungai Baru Hilir involving an allocation of approximately RM432 million as well as interventions in several other areas identified as ‘red zones.’
He explained that a ‘micro-management’ approach is being employed, where the specific issues of each area are examined to ensure that the planned solutions directly address the root causes of the flooding.
In a related development, Ab Rauf noted that the state government’s commitment to the welfare of the people is also reflected in the ‘Wakil Rakyat Untuk Rakyat’ (WRUR) programme, which is implemented across all 28 State Legislative Assembly constituencies in the state.
He shared that through this programme, 75 per cent of the approximately 4,000 issues raised by the public have been successfully resolved during his nearly three-year administration.
He added that the issues received cover a wide range of areas including education, welfare, land, agriculture, and facilities for places of worship which are then coordinated according to the portfolios of the relevant State Executive Council (MMKN) members.
“My principle as an elected representative is that we must understand the hardships faced by the people. To be an elected representative, one must first be one of the people; only then can we truly understand how to resolve the people’s problems,” he said.
Ab Rauf said in addition to WRUR, the state government also implements the ‘Exco Meets the People’ (HEBAT) programme every 45 days, serving as an additional platform to address complaints that require more serious attention from the state administration.
Furthermore, he noted that the ‘Chief Minister’s ‘Sayang Rakyat’ (MeSRa) Tour’ programme is used to evaluate the effectiveness of the aid provided to the public and to identify areas for improvement. — Bernama

Title: Sabah’s next big question: Expand KKIA, or build a brand-new airport?
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Nov 9 — Sabah’s long-term aviation needs require careful consideration of whether Kota Kinabalu International Airport (KKIA) should be expanded at its existing site or replaced by a new airport at another location.
The two proposals were discussed by aviation experts during a public forum titled ‘The Future of Kota Kinabalu International Airport: Retain, Expand or Relocate?’, organised by the Chartered Institute of Logistics and Transport (CILT) Malaysia Sabah Section at Sabah International Convention Centre (SICC) here on Saturday.
Airport, Airline and Civil Aviation Strategy Consultant Edward Clayton said several options could be considered to increase KKIA’s capacity, including constructing a second runway, adopting an alternative runway configuration or developing a separate relief airport.
He said KKIA had recorded steady passenger growth of about 4.1 per cent annually over the past 21 years since 2005, with passenger numbers reaching approximately nine million last year.
“Are we limited to 4.1 per cent per annum? Is that the capacity that it is supposed to be? Are we happy with 4.1 per cent growth every year?” he asked, questioning whether existing infrastructure was restricting Sabah’s aviation potential.
Clayton said a second runway extending into reclaimed land was one possibility, although it would involve challenges related to construction costs, environmental impact, runway spacing, surrounding terrain and operational procedures.
“An alternative runway configuration could also be considered, but the surrounding mountains and geographical constraints would require further investigation.
“Another option was to develop a separate relief airport to provide operational resilience when KKIA’s runway was unavailable. However, its viability would depend on passenger demand, investment and the distance between the two facilities.”
He stressed that expanding KKIA would involve more than adding runway capacity, as rising passenger numbers would also require larger terminal facilities, additional aircraft stands, taxiways and improved air traffic management systems.
Meanwhile, former Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) chief executive officer Datuk Captain Chester Voo urged Sabah to consider developing a new airport elsewhere to accommodate its long-term aviation and economic ambitions.
Using the analogy of a growing family outgrowing a small studio apartment, he said KKIA had served Sabah well for about 45 years, but its location and surrounding development could limit future expansion.
“It is our home. It is our capital, state capital airport. It’s great. There’s nothing wrong with it,” he said, while stressing that the key question was whether the existing site could meet Sabah’s future needs.
Voo cited geographical constraints, including the surrounding terrain and Gaya Island, as factors to consider when assessing runway safety, aircraft departure paths and future operational capacity.
He also highlighted the importance of operational resilience, citing a runway closure in September that disrupted airport operations and demonstrated the risks of relying on a single runway.
“An airport is not just about planes taking off and landing,” he said, adding that a new facility could accommodate aircraft maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO), cold-chain storage, cargo sorting centres and warehouses.
Such facilities could strengthen Sabah’s aviation and logistics industries, particularly its seafood export sector, which he said faced limitations due to the lack of dedicated cold-chain facilities at airports in the state.
Voo also proposed an airport-city or aerotropolis concept incorporating hotels, restaurants, commercial developments and other businesses to generate wider economic opportunities.
He said the existing KKIA site could potentially be redeveloped for commercial, tourism or other urban purposes if airport operations were eventually moved, given the rising value of land around Tanjung Aru and its surrounding areas.
However, he stressed that any proposed new site would require careful assessment of accessibility, terrain, airspace, flood risks, environmental considerations and weather conditions.
“Ideally, airport access should be within about 45 minutes.”
On estimated costs, Voo said developing KKIA with a second runway and a relief airport could require RM10 billion to RM15 billion over six years, while building a new airport could cost about RM10 billion over a comparable period.
He cited the relocation of operations from Subang Airport to Kuala Lumpur International Airport as an example of planning for long-term aviation capacity. — The Borneo Post

Title: Attorney General says ‘glaring error’ in Najib court document caused confusion
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 9 — Attorney General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar yesterday raised questions over the accuracy and scrutiny applied in preparing an official court document used as the basis for implementing Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s house arrest order.
According to
Berita Harian
(BH), Mohd Dusuki said the issue should never have arisen had the parties involved exercised greater care in reviewing the document.
He was commenting on alleged defects in the Kuala Lumpur High Court’s Order of Discharge document relating to the former prime minister’s sentence, which has drawn attention from legal practitioners.
Speaking to BH, he said the flaws identified in the document were obvious and should not have occurred within the country’s legal system.
“This should not have happened if the parties concerned had exercised due care. The error is glaring and has caused issues that should never have arisen,” he was quoted as saying.
The defects in question relate primarily to the accuracy of the legal terminology and statutory provisions used in the document.
While Mohd Dusuki did not specify the flaws he was referring to, the AGC had previously highlighted legal questions arising from the order’s implementation.
In a statement issued on Saturday, the AGC said the High Court’s Order of Discharge on Payment of Fine directed Najib’s immediate release following payment of the RM50 million fine on November 6, while also stating that he should serve the remainder of his SRC sentence under house arrest until August 23, 2028.
The AGC said this raised two possible legal interpretations requiring judicial clarification.
If the SRC sentence remains in force, the AGC said, its remaining term should be served in accordance with the conditional pardon.
However, if the court determines that Najib’s SRC sentence has legally ended, it would have to clarify whether his separate 15-year prison sentence in the 1MDB case should now begin, as that sentence was ordered to commence only after the SRC term was completed.
Meanwhile, when asked by BH about a reported audience with Sultan Ibrahim to explain legal questions arising from the implications of Najib’s payment of the RM50 million fine, Mohd Dusuki declined to comment further.
However, sources told the newspaper that the audience could take place as early as Tuesday.

Title: Fire tears through 24-door Kanowit longhouse, but all residents escape unharmed
Article:
KANOWIT, Nov 9 — A 24-door longhouse, Rumah Seliau at Sungai Tuah here, was badly damaged in a fire on Monday.
The Sarawak Fire and Rescue Department (Bomba) operations centre said it received a call about the incident at 1.39am.
“Sixteen firefighters from Kanowit and Sibu Jaya fire stations were deployed to the scene, about 46km away.
“The fire involved a permanent-structure longhouse measuring approximately 430 feet by 100 feet, with an estimated 80 per cent of the building destroyed,” it said in a statement.
It said no casualties or deaths were reported.
The fire was brought under control at 3.53am while the operation ended at 8.23am after overhaul work to ensure no remaining sources of fire or hidden embers could cause the blaze to reignite. — The Borneo Post

Title: After viral umbrella videos, Seberang Jaya Hospital assesses damage from leaks
Article:
BUTTERWORTH, Nov 9 — An assessment of the damage and the implementation of control measures are currently underway at Seberang Jaya Hospital (HSJ), following ceiling leaks caused by an extraordinary overflow of rainwater during heavy downpours and strong winds last Saturday.
In a statement today, the Penang State Health Department (JKNPP) announced that the HSJ Engineering Unit, in collaboration with the hospital’s building management concessionaire, is assessing the extent of the damage and carrying out control measures to address the situation.
“The incident, which occurred between 5.45pm and 7pm on Saturday, affected several locations across both the old building (Block A) and the new building (Block B). However, the majority of areas experiencing rainwater overflow were located within the old block of HSJ.
“The incident did not compromise patient safety or medical equipment. HSJ management has taken appropriate measures regarding patient care and the protection of medical equipment in the affected areas,” the statement read.
JKNPP also noted that the Defects Liability Period (DLP) for HSJ’s Block B ended on April 12, 2026. Throughout that period, no unusual rainwater overflow incidents such as the one that occurred last Saturday had been reported.
HSJ remains committed to ensuring that the delivery of healthcare services at the hospital is not disrupted following the incident.
Yesterday, exceptionally heavy rain accompanied by strong winds caused water to enter several buildings at HSJ due to ceiling leaks. While most of the affected structures were in the old block, some ceiling leaks also occurred in the new building.
Penang state health director Dr Zulhizzam Abdullah reportedly said the incident was unforeseen, resulting from exceptionally heavy rainfall, strong winds, and a high volume of water, which led to leaks and rainwater leaking in several areas. Nevertheless, no patients were affected by the incident.
Earlier, videos circulated online showing healthcare staff using umbrellas inside the HSJ building due to ceiling leaks caused by the heavy downpour, which left floors covered in water. — Bernama
